name: Trampolina
introduction: A growing world of discovery for children, bringing learning, exploration and creative thinking into interactive digital experiences.
audience: Children and the families and educators who support their learning. Activities are intended to accommodate different interests and stages of development, without a fixed age range.
purpose: To create opportunities to explore foundational ideas, try new approaches and enjoy the process of learning.
status: In development. Activity availability and release details will be confirmed before public access is offered.

sections.title: Planned learning areas
paragraphs: The following areas describe the platform’s planned direction. They are not a catalogue of currently released activities.

sections.title: Learning with curiosity
paragraphs: Trampolina’s educational direction emphasizes exploration and opportunities to practise. Digital activities are intended to complement the wider experiences through which children learn.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: Confirmed feature details will be added as activities are ready to share. No public download or store release is announced here.

name: Dr. Quiz
introduction: Fascinating facts, quizzes and mind-expanding challenges. Dr. Quiz is being developed as a place to explore questions, discover ideas and follow curiosity.
audience: Curious learners who enjoy discovering knowledge, thinking through questions and sharing quiz experiences with others.
purpose: To make knowledge discovery inviting through scientific facts, questions and intellectual challenges.
status: In development. The areas below describe the product direction; release availability and individual features are not yet announced here.

sections.title: Discover & Learn
paragraphs: Explore the intended discovery experience: interesting questions, accessible explanations and opportunities to learn something new.

sections.title: Quizzes and intellectual challenges
paragraphs: Quizzes are part of Dr. Quiz’s planned approach to knowledge discovery. Detailed formats and available topics will be introduced when confirmed.

sections.title: Party quiz activities
paragraphs: Shared quiz activities are part of the product direction. Participation options and play formats will be described when ready.

sections.title: Responsible discovery
paragraphs: Scientific facts need careful sourcing and clear explanations. Product information will distinguish what is established, what is uncertain and what remains under development.

name: NeuroPath
introduction: A suite of brain-training labs for memory, attention, logic and cognitive flexibility.
audience: People interested in ongoing cognitive engagement and lifelong learning, including adults exploring structured challenges at their own pace.
purpose: To provide a coherent collection of digital activities organized around different kinds of cognitive engagement.
status: In development. This website introduces the laboratories and their confirmed activity organization; it does not provide the mobile activities or announce a public release.

sections.title: Four connected laboratories
paragraphs: Explore Memory Lab, Attention Lab, Logic Lab and Flexibility Lab. Each has its own focus within the wider NeuroPath platform.

sections.title: Confirmed activity organization
items: Memory Lab contains the signature activity Memory Lab.
Logic Lab contains NeuroWeave and CodeQuest.

sections.title: Light Paths
paragraphs: Light Paths is an existing NeuroPath activity. Its laboratory category is awaiting confirmation, so it is not assigned to a laboratory here.

sections.title: Engagement with realistic expectations
paragraphs: NeuroPath is not a medical treatment. No activity is presented as clinically proven to prevent dementia, Alzheimer’s disease or cognitive decline, or to build cognitive reserve. Product-specific benefits require appropriate evidence.

name: Memory Lab
introduction: A dedicated space within NeuroPath for memory-oriented cognitive engagement.
audience: People interested in exploring memory-focused digital activities as part of their lifelong learning.
purpose: To organize memory-oriented experiences within a clear, accessible laboratory.
status: In development. Detailed activity descriptions and availability will be shared when confirmed.

sections.title: Signature activity
paragraphs: Memory Lab is the confirmed signature activity in this laboratory. Specific mechanics and release details are not announced here.

sections.title: What to expect next
paragraphs: Further information will explain the activity’s intended experience and how it fits into the NeuroPath platform. No clinical or preventive benefit is promised.

name: Attention Lab
introduction: The NeuroPath laboratory dedicated to attention-oriented cognitive engagement.
audience: People interested in exploring attention-focused challenges within the NeuroPath collection.
purpose: To give attention-oriented experiences a distinct home within the platform.
status: In development. An approved activity catalogue is not yet available for this laboratory.

sections.title: Activities under development
paragraphs: Confirmed activity names and descriptions will appear here when available.

sections.title: Our approach
paragraphs: This page introduces the laboratory’s focus. It does not claim measured improvements in attention or clinical outcomes.

name: Logic Lab
introduction: A home for logic-oriented cognitive engagement within NeuroPath.
audience: People who enjoy reasoning, considering possibilities and exploring intellectual challenges.
purpose: To bring the platform’s logic-focused experiences together in one laboratory.
status: In development. Signature activity names and placement are confirmed; mechanics and release availability will be introduced separately.

sections.title: Explore the ideas behind the activities
paragraphs: NeuroWeave and CodeQuest belong to Logic Lab. Further information about their individual experiences will be added when approved.

name: Flexibility Lab
introduction: The NeuroPath laboratory for cognitive-flexibility-oriented engagement.
audience: People interested in exploring different approaches to challenges within a lifelong learning journey.
purpose: To organize experiences around cognitive flexibility as a distinct focus of the platform.
status: In development. Approved activity details will be added as they become available.

sections.title: A laboratory taking shape
paragraphs: No specific activity catalogue is announced for Flexibility Lab yet. Future descriptions will clarify each confirmed activity and its intended experience.

sections.title: Responsible expectations
paragraphs: The laboratory’s focus describes a design direction. It is not a claim of clinically established improvements or protection against cognitive decline.
